instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Fair Exchange
cards.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll scrub that pan for two shopping trips. Remember when I taught you to bargain? Here's your chance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two trips for one pan?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've counted the pans. Now price the dried cheese. Two trips.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll soak it first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One trip, then. You're finally improving your offer. Bring detergent as well; negotiation doesn't wash it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Half an hour moving your sofa costs two hours painting my shed on Saturday. Let's see what you remember from my bargaining lessons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I paint after lunch? Saturday's my only lie-in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still counting only your inconvenience. Afternoon costs me cricket. Three hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hire a painter. But the sofa has to go up three flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to buy your way out. Two painter-hours for loading, one for stairs. Send him Saturday morning; your teacher keeps his cricket.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Technically, Yes
cards.instruction: Comply with every agreement in the narrowest possible way while insisting you honored it completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked me to move a box; it's beside the van. Done. Remember my lesson about precise instructions?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant all twenty boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. You've supplied a number. I'll move all twenty beside the van; that fulfills your request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Inside the van, please. The sofa has to fit too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put the boxes on the sofa. Both inside. You remembered space; next time remember the upholstery I taught you to protect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your fern's watered. Holiday duty complete. I taught you to ask for exactly what you need, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need every plant watered every day until Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're remembering quantities. One teaspoon per plant each day. Every word honored.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A full can on each. Empty the saucers afterwards, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're specifying the dose. I'll empty the saucers on Sunday. You only made the watering daily; write that distinction down before your next holiday.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tap drips. Time to replace the sink. I taught you to look beyond the obvious fault.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs a washer. I've already bought one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good beginner diagnosis. We'll fit it when the sink's out, then replace that swollen worktop. You used to stop after the easy part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The worktop runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There, you're finally following the problem. Empty the cupboards; we'll move them and fix the whole kitchen layout. I'll show you where to start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This café chair wobbles. Take the chairs apart; let's use the fault-finding method I taught you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tested them. It's only this chair, on this floorboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finally, a proper diagnosis. Lift the floorboards; we'll see what else your teacher has saved you from missing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're opening in twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then close for renovations. With the floor out, we'll move the counter and fix the queue. Write that on the sign, not 'Broken chair.' I taught you to look past the first fault.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make Them Your Deputy
cards.instruction: Get someone’s help by defining it as service under your direction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sold raffle tickets just as I taught you. Ready to be my deputy? I need someone to run the stall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've sold every ticket. I could run the draw with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent sales, but let's not skip a grade. You read the numbers; I'll decide when we draw.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then start now. Everyone with a ticket is waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're noticing your audience. Tell them your director has authorized the draw. Then bring me the bucket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me organize the picnic. You've learned enough from me to be second-in-command; you can choose the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Or we could share the decisions. I picked the one by the pond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly right. I taught you to check the ground: that bench is wet. Choose a dry one, then report back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The dry one's uphill. You'll have to carry the hamper with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're learning to delegate. Take that handle, deputy. We'll carry it together when I give the word.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Not Dismissed
cards.instruction: Keep someone present by treating departure as a privilege only you can grant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shop's shut, but you're not dismissed. I taught you to close this till; let's see whether it stuck.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cash counted, drawer locked. My daughter's waiting outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remembered the easy bits. Bring her in while you show me the closing report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I sent you the report. Our taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Efficient—finally. I'll read it beside your taxi. Keep the door open; if you've followed my method, I should be able to release you before the meter hurts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coat off a moment. I taught you a proper goodbye; you haven't thanked me for the coffee yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you for the coffee. My bus is due.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. Now try it without watching the door. I'll tell you when you've finished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The café's closing. They've asked us both to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll practise outside. You can thank the waiter on the way; I taught you that too. Then come back to me for permission to go.
